note: The raw fuzz input is copied into the stack-allocated lexer input buffer and lexer.inbuflen is set to the input size.
The parser consumes the copied bytes in-place from lexer.inbuffer.
The first 0xd3 byte enters the RTCM3 recognizer, but the following 0xff byte is rejected by the high-bit check and the stale 0xd3 remains in inbuffer.
Because 0xff has nonzero high six bits, this apparent RTCM3 header is rejected and parsing continues without discarding the stale preamble bytes from the buffer.
A later valid 0xd3 00 00 sequence passes the RTCM3 length high-bit check.
The valid RTCM3 frame declares a zero payload length.
The recognizer waits only for the declared payload plus three checksum bytes before setting RTCM3_RECOGNIZED.
After three checksum bytes for the later valid frame, the parser reaches RTCM3_RECOGNIZED.
Final validation scans from the beginning of inbuffer and selects the stale earlier 0xd3 rather than the later valid frame that caused recognition.
The stale bytes after the first 0xd3 are interpreted as an unmasked 0xffff RTCM3 length.
crc24q_check is called with a length derived from stale bytes, causing a read far beyond the bytes present in the stack lexer buffer.
